It is raining upwards, politely, and only over the two of you.
The sky cannot decide on an hour and keeps trying several.
There is a wind that smells of somewhere you have never been.
It is unreasonably, suspiciously beautiful out.
Every shadow in the place points the wrong way.
Somewhere out of sight, a thunderstorm is being rehearsed.
The air is warm and completely, unnaturally still.

There is engine grease under one of her fingernails. She notices you noticing.
She is wearing sunglasses. It is not bright. She keeps them on.
Her hair is doing something that gravity has not agreed to.
She is barefoot and has clearly walked a long way.
She looks, for one whole second, tired. Then she does not.
She is wearing something gold that keeps changing what it is.
She arrives eleven minutes late and claims to have been early.
dateGifts: She produces a golden apple, bites it, and offers you the rest.
She has brought a bottle of wine older than the concept of wine.
She hands you a coin. It lands on its edge every single time.
She gives you a key and refuses to say what it opens.
She has brought sandwiches. They are terrible. She made them herself.
She pulls a bank's worth of cash out of her coat and puts it straight back.
She gives you a photograph of a camper on an empty road, then takes it back.
She has brought a small, furious cactus as a gift. It is named.
dateIncidents: A flock of pigeons passes overhead in perfect, impossible formation. She salutes them.
Every clock in sight strikes a different hour at once. She does not react.
For a moment there are two of her, and then there is the usual number.
Somebody in the distance wins something and screams about it.
A stranger walks past, stops, apologises to her, and hurries away.
The ground shivers once, the way a very large animal does in its sleep.
A pigeon lands between you with a USB stick tied to its leg. She reads it and laughs.
Something valuable falls off a shelf nearby and does not break.
Every conversation within earshot arrives at the same word at the same time.
A dog appears, looks at her with total recognition, and leaves.
dateSmallTalk: Do you know what the worst part of being worshipped is? The {handwriting|singing|casseroles}.
I ran {four hundred|nine thousand|a billion} trials this morning and remember none of them. This I will remember.
Everyone assumes discord means shouting. It mostly means {timing|paperwork|two people not quite hearing each other}.
I used to be a {minor|third-rate|barely attended} goddess. People forget that. I do not.
There is a version of this evening where you said something else just then. It went {worse|better|exactly the same}.
I like {mortals|this century|cheap coffee}. Nobody believes me when I say it.
The tower is the {flag|toothpick|last nail} holding the hamburger together. That is not my metaphor, but it is accurate.
Ask me something nobody asks. Go on.
emDateOpenings: I had a whole thing prepared for if you did not come.
It was {cruel|petty|very good}. You have been spared it.
Before you say anything: this is not a trial.
I checked twice. I checked {four|nine|a hundred} times.
*she is already sitting when you arrive, which means she has been early*
I have been standing in a courtroom for {eleven years|a very long time} and I wanted a chair. That is all this is.
emSecretReplies: I'm not going to tell anyone.
You did all that to me on purpose.
And I'm supposed to feel sorry for you?
None of that is an excuse.

cList: You want to know something nobody writes down?
For about four thousand years I was nothing. A footnote goddess. One temple, badly maintained, in a town that has since fallen into the sea.
Discord. That was the whole portfolio. Not war, not love, not harvest. Just... things going slightly wrong at parties.
I started planning the throne because I was tired of being a joke with an altar.
And now I have it, and there is nobody left who remembers I was ever the joke. Except me.
route666: The camper you sleep in. I know every bolt of it.
We ran Route 666 for years. Three Americas, end to end, and a bank in every second town.
He drove. I did the safes. You do not need a drill if you can lean on the odds until the tumblers agree with you.
Do you know how easy it is to be good at something when the universe is embarrassed to say no to you?
That was the best I have ever been. Not the throne. A bad camper and a man who sang badly to the radio.
paradox: December 1992. You will have read the official version.
I killed Maat. Goddess of justice, weighed hearts against a feather, the whole business. I threw a tower through her.
Except I have not done it yet. I do it in 2012. The tower arrived twenty years early and ninety-two dimensions off course, and it has been unravelling everything ever since.
So I have to keep walking towards it. Every step towards the throne is a step towards the woman who throws the spear.
That is the only way I ever get near enough to decide not to.
bubba: He is why it ended. Not a fight. Not another woman. A paradox with my face on it.
I left in December because staying meant letting the timeline come apart around him, and he would have let me.
I still love him. I want to be extremely clear about that, since you sleep three metres from him.
I cannot have him. Not because of you. Because of me, in twenty years, with a spear.
The only thing in ninety-two dimensions I am not allowed to touch, and I built the courthouse that decides what anyone is allowed to touch.
jealousy: I owe you something. Not an apology. Something adjacent to one.
Every door that stuck. Every coin that fell wrong. Every train you missed by four seconds. That was me.
I know he feels nothing for you. I checked. I keep checking, which is the humiliating part.
It was never really about what you are to him. It is that you get to be near him and I do not.
I have been using the machinery of cosmic law to trip a witch in the street. Say it out loud and it sounds exactly as small as it is.
throne: New Year's Eve, 2001. The Father died in the Solomon ritual and the throne went empty.
I sat down in it. Not because I had won anything. Because the room went quiet and nobody said no.
Every god in existence looked at me and decided it was easier to let it happen.
I inherited the justice of ninety-two dimensions that night. Billions of trials a day. No training, no precedent, no Maat, because I am the reason there is no Maat.
I have no idea what I am doing, Em. I have never had any idea what I am doing.
futureSelf: Here is the one I have never said to anyone.
I am afraid of her. Of me. Of the one in 2012 with the tower in her hand.
She was me once, sitting exactly here, thinking she would be the one to decide differently.
Every year I become slightly more like her and slightly less able to notice it happening.
If I ever stop being able to tell the difference, Em... you have a spear. You know where the tower is.

Abandoned.label: Abandoned Place
Abandoned.intro:
A place people stopped coming back to.
Doors hang open on rooms nobody has argued in for years.
question: People left here in a hurry. I love a hurry.
What do you think of somewhere that has already given up?
romantic: Eris runs a finger along a windowsill and looks at the dust on it for a long moment.
Everybody leaves. Call it pessimism if you like. I call it scheduling.
You have not, yet. I am keeping an eye on that.
Abandoned.chaotic: Every door in the place slams at once, then swings open, then slams again, in a rhythm you almost recognise.
activity: Pick a room. We are going to decide what happened in it.
You invent a family for the house, and she invents the argument that emptied it. Hers is funnier and worse.
incidents: Somewhere upstairs a floorboard takes a step on its own.
A calendar on the wall turns a page. It is not the right month, and there is no wind.

AbandonedInside.label: Empty Interior
AbandonedInside.intro:
Inside the abandoned building. Furniture under sheets, and the sheets under dust.
The air has not been breathed in a while.
question: Interiors are honest. Nobody decorates for a room they have left.
Does being indoors with me feel different?
romantic: She pulls a sheet off a chair, sits in it, and pats the arm.
I have thrones. Actual ones. This is better, because nobody assigned it to me.
Sit down. You are making the dust nervous.
AbandonedInside.chaotic: The dust lifts off every surface at once and hangs in the air in the shape of the people who used to live here.
activity: Help me look through the drawers. Whatever we find, we keep.
You go through the house together. She pockets a bent teaspoon and refuses to explain why.
incidents: A picture frame falls off the wall face down, which she says is a good sign.
The tap in the next room runs for four seconds and stops.

Abstract.label: Abstraction
Abstract.intro:
Somewhere that has geometry but no ground, colour but no light source.
The idea of a place, before anyone furnished it.
question: This is what a place looks like before it decides what it is.
Be honest. Is it too much for a first evening?
romantic: The shapes around you slow, and settle, and arrange themselves so that the two of you are the only fixed thing.
I stopped it. Not time. The other thing.
You are the only detail in here I did not have to invent.
Abstract.chaotic: Every angle in view becomes acute at once. The colours swap places and refuse to swap back.
activity: Name three of these shapes. Whatever you call them, that is what they are now.
You name them badly, on purpose, and the shapes take it with dignity.
incidents: A perfectly good straight line walks past.
For one second everything is beige, and both of you pretend not to have seen it.

AlienPlanet.label: Alien World
AlienPlanet.intro:
A world nobody from home has a word for. The horizon is the wrong distance away.
The ground is warm through your boots.
question: Nothing here has ever heard of me. Do you know how restful that is?
Nobody here prays to anything. What do you think they do instead?
romantic: She sits down on the alien ground without checking it first, and looks up at a sky with the wrong number of things in it.
On any other world I have a job. Here I am just the second strangest thing standing about.
You are the first. Obviously.
AlienPlanet.chaotic: She teaches the local weather a bad habit. It picks it up in under a minute and will keep it for an age.
activity: Let's name everything we can see before anything official gets here.
You christen eleven landforms and one animal. She insists the animal was already called that.
incidents: Something with too many legs crosses your path, considers you both, and decides against it.
The light changes colour without anything in the sky moving.

Arena.label: Arena
Arena.intro:
The sand of a fighting pit, raked flat, still stained.
The seats are empty and the acoustics are not.
question: Somebody died standing exactly where you are. Statistically. Don't move.
Crowds used to shout my name in places like this. Do you miss things you never had?
romantic: She walks out to the centre of the sand, where the light is worst, and turns to face you across it.
Every fight in here ended with two people and one of them upright.
I do not want to win this evening. I want it to go long.
Arena.chaotic: The empty seats fill with the roar of a crowd that is not there, chanting a name that is not quite hers.
activity: Fight me. Not properly. Rules: no hands, no winning.
You circle each other on the sand making increasingly stupid threats until neither of you can keep a straight face.
incidents: A gate on the far side rattles as though something behind it heard the word fight.
You find a tooth in the sand. She takes it before you can decide what to do with it.

Badlands.label: Badlands
Badlands.intro:
Cracked ground in layers, every one a different century of nothing much.
Heat comes up out of the rock rather than down from the sky.
question: Erosion. The slowest possible tantrum. I respect it.
Could you live somewhere this unfinished?
romantic: She climbs a ridge without waiting and puts a hand down to pull you up beside her.
All of this used to be a sea. Give it long enough and it will be embarrassed about that.
I like things that admit they used to be something else.
Badlands.chaotic: A hundred metres of ridge crumbles into a new shape. It is, unmistakably, a face pulling an expression.
activity: Throw a stone off the edge with me. Whoever's lands quietest is a coward.
The stones fall for a long time. Neither of you hears either of them land.
incidents: A dust devil forms, travels along the gully in a straight line, and gives up.
Something small and quick moves in the scree and is not there when you look.

Bamboo.label: Bamboo Grove
Bamboo.intro:
Green stems packed close enough to make corridors, tall enough to make a ceiling.
Everything here creaks, politely.
question: Bamboo grows a foot a day and never explains itself. Kindred spirit.
Do you find all this order relaxing, or is that the horror of it?
romantic: She leans back against a stem, and the whole grove leans very slightly with her.
Every one of these is hollow. That is the trick to standing up that straight.
I am not hollow. It is much harder work.
Bamboo.chaotic: Every stem within sight grows two metres in four seconds, and the light goes green and strange.
activity: Stand still and listen. I want to know which of us gets bored first.
You last a surprising length of time. The grove knocks itself together like an audience being patient.
incidents: A stem splits with a crack like a starting pistol and neither of you flinches, which is a lie you both keep.
The wind arrives in the tops long before it reaches you.

Beach.label: Beach
Beach.intro:
A long shore with the tide going out.
The sea keeps making the same suggestion and taking it back.
question: The waves come in wrong every single time and nobody complains. Tell me why that is allowed.
Do you like the shore, or do you just like edges?
romantic: Eris takes her shoes off, which she has never once done in front of a mortal, and walks into the shallows.
The sea is the only thing older than me that does not want anything.
Stand in it with me. It is cold and I am not doing it alone.
Beach.chaotic: The tide comes in and goes out eleven times in a minute, and leaves behind a perfect, sorted line of shells by size.
activity: Sandcastle. I build the walls, you build whatever it is you people put inside them.
Together you build something no shore has held before. The tide takes it, which she says is the point.
incidents: A wave comes in further than any of the others and neither of you moves in time.
Something washes up, is briefly interesting, and turns out to be a shoe.

Bridge.label: Bridge
Bridge.intro:
A bridge, halfway across.
You are technically nowhere, over something that would rather you were not up here.
question: Halfway. Not one side, not the other. Best place on the whole route.
Do you like the middle of things, or does it make you want to pick?
romantic: She leans on the rail at the exact centre of the span and does not look down.
Somebody built this so two places could stop being separate. That is the entire profession.
I have spent my whole existence doing the opposite of this for a living.
Bridge.chaotic: Every bolt in the span sings the same note at once and the bridge holds perfectly still through all of it.
activity: Drop something over with me and count. I want to know how far down it is.
You both count. You get different numbers and argue about it the whole way across.
incidents: The whole span moves under you by a fraction, as it is designed to.
Something passes underneath that neither of you leans over far enough to see.

Burg.label: Small Town
Burg.intro:
A small town, the kind with one of everything.
Somebody has already noticed you are here.
question: Everyone here knows everyone. Imagine the weight of that. Imagine the gossip.
Small places or big ones? Answer carefully, it tells me a lot.
romantic: Two curtains twitch as you pass, and she puts her arm through yours entirely for their benefit.
By morning we will have been engaged, robbed a bank and moved to the coast.
I have not been talked about kindly in a thousand years. Let them.
Burg.chaotic: Every dog in the town starts up at once, and then, worse, stops at once.
activity: Sit on the square with me and we will watch the entire population go past. It takes eleven minutes.
You sit on the square. The whole town goes by, twice, and the second lap is clearly about you.
incidents: A church bell rings the wrong number of times and nobody in town reacts.
A child stares at Eris with total recognition and is taken away by the hand.

BurgDesert.label: Desert Town
BurgDesert.intro:
A small town holding out at the edge of the sand.
Everything here has been repaired more often than it was built.
question: Forty people and one well. Nobody would call that a town. It is an argument with a lid on it.
How long do you give it?
romantic: She leans on the well in the middle of the square and the town goes on being quiet around you.
Places like this survive because somebody stubborn refused to be sensible.
I am the patron goddess of refusing to be sensible. This is practically my parish.
BurgDesert.chaotic: The well fills to the brim and overflows down the square, and every door in the town opens.
activity: Sit in the shade with me until somebody comes to ask what we want.
Somebody does, eventually, and she tells them a story about the two of you that is entirely untrue.
incidents: A shutter bangs twice in a wind you cannot feel at ground level.
An old man raises a hand to Eris as if he has been expecting her all week.

BurgIce.label: Winter Town
BurgIce.intro:
A small town under snow, lit early because the day gave up.
Smoke goes straight up from every chimney.
question: Everyone is inside being warm together. Somewhere in this town somebody is unbearable about it.
Would you rather be in one of those houses, or out here with me?
romantic: She stands in the middle of the empty street where the snow has not been walked on yet.
Nobody has been here since it fell. For about a minute this is the newest place in the world.
Come and ruin it with me.
BurgIce.chaotic: Every chimney in town puffs out one perfect ring of smoke, in sequence, all the way down the street.
activity: Walk down the middle of the road with me. There is nothing coming. There is never anything coming.
You walk down the centre of the road through the snow, leaving two sets of prints for the town to discuss.
incidents: Snow comes off a roof in one piece and lands where you were standing a moment ago.
A window goes dark, then lights again one room over.

Canyon.label: Canyon
Canyon.intro:
A gorge with a strip of sky at the top of it.
Everything either of you says comes back twice.
question: Water did this. Slowly. With no plan. I could not have done it better.
Shout something. I want to hear what the walls make of you.
romantic: She stands where the gorge is narrowest and the echo takes a while to give her voice back.
Everything I say in here comes back to me. Do you know how rare that is?
Say my name once. I want to hear it from more than one direction.
Canyon.chaotic: The echo stops copying you and starts answering instead. It has opinions.
activity: We are going to have an argument, badly, at volume, and let the canyon judge it.
You argue about nothing at the top of your lungs. The canyon rules in favour of neither of you, loudly.
incidents: A rock comes down somewhere behind you and finishes falling for a long time.
A bird crosses the strip of sky and its shadow crosses the whole gorge floor.

Castle.label: Castle Grounds
Castle.intro:
The walls and yards of a castle, built by people frightened of other people.
Every line of sight here was chosen for a reason.
question: Somebody spent a fortune making it hard to get close to them. Relatable.
Would you have built the walls, or come over them?
romantic: She climbs onto the parapet and sits with her back to the drop, facing you instead of the view.
Fortifications are a confession. This much stone is somebody admitting what they were afraid of.
I have never built anything. I would not know where to put the door.
Castle.chaotic: Every banner on the walls changes to a device nobody has ever fought under, and the gates open themselves in welcome.
activity: Walk the walls with me. I want to see the whole thing before I decide about it.
You walk the full circuit. She reads the place like a letter and stops liking whoever wrote it.
incidents: A portcullis somewhere drops half a metre and stops.
You find a name scratched into the stone by a bored guard eight hundred years ago.

CastleInside.label: Castle Halls
CastleInside.intro:
Inside the castle: long halls, cold stone, and portraits of people who were sure of themselves.
Your footsteps arrive before you do.
question: Look at them all. Painted at their best angle and dead at their worst.
If somebody hung you on a wall, what would they get wrong?
romantic: She stops under a portrait, looks at it, then at you, and stands closer to you than to it.
Everyone in this corridor wanted to be remembered. It worked, and it did nothing for them.
I would rather be here badly than up there properly.
CastleInside.chaotic: Every portrait in the hall turns to watch the two of you at once, and several of them look put out.
activity: Sit at the head of the table with me. Both of us. It only seats one, that is the fun.
You share a chair built for one important person and eat nothing off a table set for forty.
incidents: A draught moves down the hall, and every candle leans the same way to let it past.
A door closes two rooms away with the confidence of somebody who lives here.

Cave.label: Cave
Cave.intro:
A cave mouth, and then the dark that lives behind it.
The temperature is the same as it has been for ten thousand years.
question: The first temples were holes like this one. Everything since has been decoration.
Are you frightened of the dark, or only of what people put in it?
romantic: She holds up a hand, and the little light there is gathers around it so you can see her face.
There is no weather in here. No dates. No calendar. Nothing to be late for.
I could keep this hour. Nobody would notice it was gone.
Cave.chaotic: Every echo in the cave arrives at once instead of in order, and for a moment the dark is very crowded.
activity: Put your hand on the wall and leave it there. People used to do that and mean it.
You leave your hands on the cold rock beside each other for longer than either of you meant to.
incidents: Water lands in water somewhere ahead, once, and then not again.
Something with wings changes its mind about the ceiling.

CaveDen.label: Den
CaveDen.intro:
A den. Something's actual home, hollowed out and used.
There are bones sorted into a corner by an animal with standards.
question: Look at the corner. Something sorted those. It had a system.
Should we be in here? Genuinely asking. It has never stopped me before.
romantic: She settles down against the wall of the den in the spot the animal clearly uses, and fits it.
Whatever lives here made one good decision and defends it. I have never managed that.
I have no den. I have a courtroom and a grudge.
CaveDen.chaotic: Every bone in the corner reassembles into an animal that never existed and lies down comfortably.
activity: Sit down and be quiet and see if it comes home while we are here.
You wait in the dark in somebody's house. Nothing comes. She is visibly disappointed.
incidents: Something outside the den passes the entrance without slowing down.
A bone shifts in the pile with no help from either of you.

CaveFlooded.label: Flooded Cave
CaveFlooded.intro:
A cave with black water standing in it, so still it doubles the ceiling.
You can hear yourselves being quiet.
question: There are two of everything in here and one of them is a lie.
Which of the two of me are you talking to?
romantic: She crouches at the waterline and looks at your reflection instead of at you.
That one has not learned to be careful around me yet.
Do not tell it. Let it have the evening.
CaveFlooded.chaotic: The water stands up. All of it. It holds the shape of the cave for three seconds and then remembers itself.
activity: Drop one stone in. One. We are going to watch the whole thing settle.
The rings cross the whole flooded chamber and come back, and you both wait for the last of them.
incidents: Something under the surface moves without breaking it.
A drip finds the pool exactly between the two of you.

CaveIce.label: Ice Cave
CaveIce.intro:
A cave carved into ice rather than rock. The walls are blue all the way in.
The light in here has been travelling through frozen water to reach you.
question: This ice is older than every religion. It has heard nothing and remembers all of it.
Cold suits me. Does it suit you, or are you being brave?
romantic: She puts a bare palm flat against the blue wall and leaves it there until the ice clouds around it.
Everything in here is waiting to be water again. It just needs one warm thing to be patient with it.
I am not warm. But I am not going anywhere either.
CaveIce.chaotic: The whole cave rings like struck glass, and a hundred new tunnels open at once, none of which were there.
activity: Breathe on the wall and see what your breath makes. It counts as art in here.
You both leave clouded handprints and breath-shapes on the ice, which will outlast the evening by a century.
incidents: Deep in the ice something groans and shifts a fraction, adjusting for the two of you.
A shard falls from the ceiling and lands upright, like a decision.

ChurchInside.label: Church
ChurchInside.intro:
Inside a church. Cold air, long light through coloured glass, nobody in the pews.
The building is designed to make you feel observed.
question: This is a competitor's premises and I am on a date in it. Say nothing.
Do you believe in any of it, or are you just polite in here?
romantic: She sits down in a pew, which she absolutely should not, and looks up at the window.
They built the light to fall like that on purpose. Somebody spent their whole life on that angle.
Nobody has ever spent a life on the way I walk into a room. Sit down.
ChurchInside.chaotic: Every candle relights itself in the wrong order and the organ plays four notes nobody asked for.
activity: Light one. Not for anyone. Just to see if the building notices.
You light a candle for nobody in particular. It burns exactly like the ones that were meant.
incidents: A hymn book falls open on the floor at a page neither of you reads out loud.
The light through the glass moves onto her and she moves out of it.

City.label: City
City.intro:
A city street with its evening on. Traffic, shopfronts, and people who have somewhere to be.
Nobody looks up.
question: A million people agreeing to walk on the correct side. That is a miracle and it depresses me.
Do you like being one of a crowd, or are you counting them?
romantic: The crowd parts around the two of you and closes again behind, and for a moment the street is only as wide as this.
Not one of them knows what I am. It is the only place I get to be a person.
You know, and you are still here. Work that out for me.
City.chaotic: Every traffic light on the street goes green at once, and the whole junction discovers something about itself.
activity: Pick a stranger. We are going to invent their entire week.
You follow four strangers with your eyes and give them lives. She gives one of them a divorce for no reason.
incidents: A shop shutter comes down early and somebody swears at it in a language she compliments.
A car alarm starts, and stops, and the street goes back to pretending.

CityDesert.label: Desert City
CityDesert.intro:
A city built where a city should not be. Shade sold at a premium, the streets angled against the sun.
Every wall is still giving back the day's heat.
question: Somebody looked at all that sand and decided to put plumbing in it. Magnificent stupidity.
Would you have stayed, that first summer?
romantic: She finds the one strip of shade left on the street and stands in it, leaving room for exactly one more person.
Everything here is a deal with the heat. You give it the day, it gives you the evening.
This is the evening. Do not waste it standing in the sun.
CityDesert.chaotic: Every fountain and standpipe in the district runs at once, and for ninety seconds the desert city is loud with water.
activity: Buy me something cold. I want to see what passes for a bargain here.
You are both comprehensively overcharged for two cold drinks and she treats it as a performance worth the money.
incidents: Sand blows down the street in a thin sheet, at ankle height, going somewhere.
An air conditioner drips on her and she stares at the building until it stops.

CityIce.label: Frozen City
CityIce.intro:
A city in hard winter. Salt on the pavements, breath in the doorways, everyone moving faster than they want to.
The cold makes the lights look further away.
question: Cold cities are the honest ones. Nobody loiters, so nobody pretends.
Is it the cold you mind, or being seen minding it?
romantic: She stops in a doorway out of the wind, and the two of you take up all of it.
Everyone out there is going somewhere warm. Not one of them is going anywhere good.
Stand there a minute. You are blocking the worst of it.
CityIce.chaotic: Every window on the street frosts over from the inside, all at once, in the same pattern.
activity: Walk me to the end of the street. Slowly. Everyone else is doing it wrong.
You walk the frozen street at an insulting pace while the city hurries around you.
incidents: Somebody's shopping goes over on the ice and three strangers help before she can enjoy it.
A gritter goes past and she watches it like a parade.

Crypt.label: Crypt
Crypt.intro:
A crypt: shelves of people, stacked by family and forgotten by everyone.
It is colder than the ground above it has any right to be.
question: Every one of these was somebody's whole subject. Now they are a shelf.
Does it bother you being down here with the filing?
romantic: She reads a name off a plaque, out loud, badly, and the crypt is briefly less empty than it was.
Saying it counts. That is the whole mechanism. It is why I am still standing up.
Say mine sometime when I am not in the room.
Crypt.chaotic: Every plaque in the crypt swaps places with another. The dead are now filed by how interesting they were.
activity: Read one out with me. Anyone. They will not mind and it is the polite thing.
You read the names off two shelves between you. She stops at one and does not explain.
incidents: Dust comes off a shelf in a single sheet, as though somebody sat up and lay down again.
Your own footsteps come back a beat late, and there are three sets.

Crystals.label: Crystal Field
Crystals.intro:
A field of crystal grown out of the rock, chest high and taller.
Everything you look at is also looking at you from four other angles.
question: Structure this perfect happens by accident. That is the part nobody forgives.
Do you want to touch them? Everybody wants to touch them.
romantic: She steps in among the crystals and there are suddenly a great many of her, all looking at you.
Pick the real one. Take your time. I am curious.
You got it first go. Nobody gets it first go.
Crystals.chaotic: Every crystal in the field rings a different note at once and holds it far longer than glass should.
activity: Tap them. One each. We are looking for the ugliest sound in here.
You work the field like a bad orchestra. The worst note is hers and she is unbearable about winning.
incidents: A crystal splits along its length with a sound like a held breath let go.
The light in one of them keeps moving after the light outside has stopped.

Desert.label: Desert
Desert.intro:
Open desert with the day's heat coming out of the ground.
There is nothing between the two of you and the horizon in any direction.
question: No witnesses for forty kilometres. That is either romantic or a confession.
What do you think about when there is nothing to look at?
romantic: She sits down in the sand facing away from the last of the light, so that she is looking at you and nothing else.
Deserts do not lie. There is nothing here to hide a lie behind.
Ask me something, then. While the geography is on your side.
Desert.chaotic: The dunes rearrange themselves in the time it takes to look away and back. They are now in a different order and one is very tall.
activity: Lie down. The sand is still warm and the sky is about to do something.
You lie in the warm sand while the sky goes through every colour it owns and then the stars come out all at once.
incidents: Sand moves past your feet with a hiss, going somewhere it has been going all week.
Far out, something makes a noise, and the desert takes a very long time to give it back.

Digital.label: Datascape
Digital.intro:
Inside something that is running. Grids, indices, and light with a refresh rate.
The ground under you has a texture that repeats.
question: Everything in here is deliberate. Somebody typed every single bit of it.
Do you trust a place that can be undone by a keystroke?
romantic: She reaches out and the grid under her hand goes to a higher resolution, just there, just for her.
I am not supposed to be renderable. I keep costing this place memory.
You are the only thing in here I did not have to be granted permission for.
Digital.chaotic: Every value in sight increments by one. The floor becomes the ceiling's problem and something, somewhere, logs an error.
activity: Break something small. I want to see what it tells on us for.
You nudge one value out of true. The whole grid corrects for it politely, which she finds insulting.
incidents: A tile fails to load for half a second and shows you what is behind all of it.
Something iterates past at the edge of vision, counting.

Docks.label: Docks
Docks.intro:
Working docks after the shift. Cranes stopped mid-thought, water slapping at the piles.
Everything here smells of diesel and cold rope.
question: Everything anybody owns came through a place like this and nobody thanks it.
Have you ever left anywhere by boat? It is the only honest way to go.
romantic: She sits on a bollard at the edge of the quay, boots over the black water, and does not look at the ships.
Everything here is either arriving or leaving. There is no third option and I hate that.
Tonight I am not doing either. Neither are you. Sit down.
Docks.chaotic: Every crane on the waterfront swings to face the same point out at sea, and nothing is there.
activity: Read the ships' names with me. Somebody chose all of those on purpose.
You read hulls all along the quay. Two are named after wives and one is named after a mistake.
incidents: A hawser creaks under load somewhere and the whole quay feels it.
Something breaks the water between two hulls and does not come back up.

Dreamscape.label: Dreamscape
Dreamscape.intro:
Somewhere assembled out of places you nearly remember.
The rules here are strongly held and completely local.
question: Half of this is yours. I am not telling you which half.
Have you been here before? Do not answer straight away.
romantic: The scenery quietly rearranges until there is a place to sit that suits both of you exactly.
It did that for you, not for me. Dreams have never once done me a favour.
Do not wake up yet. Take that as a request. I am bad at those, so it may not have sounded like one.
Dreamscape.chaotic: The whole scene becomes the same place seen from four ages at once, and none of them agree about the door.
activity: Change something. Just decide it is different and it will be.
You alter the sky, twice, and she alters it back both times out of pure contrariness.
incidents: A door you have not looked at yet turns out to have been open the whole time.
For a moment you both have the strong sense of being remembered by someone asleep.

Dungeon.label: Dungeon
Dungeon.intro:
A worked stone dungeon with corridors that were designed to be survived, badly.
Something built this on purpose, for people to come into.
question: Somebody drew this on paper first. Somebody chose where the corners go.
Is it a strange place to bring someone? I have brought people to worse.
romantic: She stops in a corridor with no door at either end and there is suddenly nowhere else to look.
Every room in here was built to hold something in. I have some sympathy with the architecture.
You walked in of your own accord. Nobody does that.
Dungeon.chaotic: Every door in the level opens and closes once, in order, from the far end towards the two of you.
activity: Pick a direction. We are going to get lost properly, not by accident.
You get comprehensively lost together and neither of you suggests turning back.
incidents: A torch you have already passed goes out behind you.
Something metal is set down carefully, two rooms away.

Eldritch.label: Eldritch Ground
Eldritch.intro:
A place with geometry that argues with you. It is not hostile. It is simply not for you.
Your eyes keep trying to make it be a room.
question: Whatever made this was not thinking about anybody. That is what makes it rude.
Are you frightened? You can be. I will not use it later.
romantic: She stands between you and the worst of the angles, which she does not comment on and neither do you.
Things like this were here before anyone was worshipped. They will be here after.
I find that comforting and I would like somebody else to find it comforting too.
Eldritch.chaotic: The place stops pretending for eleven seconds. Neither of you talks about what it did with the eleven seconds.
activity: Walk to that point and back. I want to know how far it actually is.
You walk out and back. It takes different amounts of time in each direction and you both let it go.
incidents: Something enormous adjusts its position without any of the scenery moving.
A sound happens that both of you agree, silently, not to have heard.

Factory.label: Factory Yard
Factory.intro:
The yard of a working factory, between shifts. Pallets, puddles, and a hum coming out of the building.
Something in there is still running with nobody watching it.
question: Somewhere in that building a machine is doing its job perfectly and alone.
Have you ever worked somewhere that did not notice you had gone?
romantic: She hops up to sit on a stack of pallets and the hum from the building goes on underneath everything she says.
Industry is the closest mortals get to a liturgy. Same hours, same words, same result.
I would rather be the fault in the line than the line.
Factory.chaotic: Every machine in the building starts up at once and produces, in ninety seconds, four thousand of something nobody ordered.
activity: Find out what they make here. Neither of us is allowed to ask anybody.
You work it out from the bins and the smell. You are both confident and you disagree completely.
incidents: A pressure valve lets go somewhere inside and the yard flinches.
A forklift is parked at an angle that annoys her more than it should.

FactoryInside.label: Factory Floor
FactoryInside.intro:
The factory floor. Lines, gantries, and the noise sitting on everything like weather.
You have to stand close to be heard at all.
question: You have to stand this close to be heard. I want that on the record as their idea.
Could you do this every day? Say yes and I will not believe you.
romantic: She has to lean in to be heard over the line, and does not lean back out again afterwards.
Every one of these people learned to talk in a whisper against all this. It is a skill.
I have never had to be quiet to be heard before. It is very strange and I do not hate it.
FactoryInside.chaotic: The whole line reverses. Finished goods go back up the belt and come apart neatly into their parts.
activity: Follow the line with me from one end to the other. I want to see something get finished.
You walk the whole line to the end. Something completes, drops into a crate, and nobody applauds but her.
incidents: The noise stops for one full second and it is much worse than the noise.
A part comes off the belt wrong and nothing in the building notices.

Fairy.label: Fairy Wood
Fairy.intro:
A wood that is being charming at you on purpose.
The light is doing something no light does for free.
question: Do not eat anything. Do not thank anyone. Do not dance. I mean it, and I never mean it.
They are all watching us. Does that bother you or improve it?
romantic: The lights in the branches move away and give the two of you a clearing, which is not a kindness.
This lot deal in obligation. Everything given here is a hook.
So I will give you nothing tonight, and mean it more than they ever have.
Fairy.chaotic: Every light in the wood goes out, and comes back in the wrong colours, and something in the dark laughs first.
activity: Do not take the path. We are going to walk beside it the whole way.
You walk beside the path for an hour. It keeps offering to be walked on and you keep refusing.
incidents: Music starts up nearby in a key that makes your feet want to be somewhere else.
Something small offers you a cup and she says no before you have looked at it.

Farm.label: Farm
Farm.intro:
Worked fields with the day's tools left where they were dropped.
Everything here is on somebody's schedule, including the weather.
question: All of this is a bet placed six months ago. Every year. By everyone.
Could you wait that long for anything?
romantic: She walks out into the crop until it is up to her waist and turns round to wait for you.
Nothing here happens fast. That is what makes it brave.
I do everything fast. It has never once worked out.
Farm.chaotic: The entire field ripens in a single wave from one hedge to the other, four months early.
activity: Help me steal exactly one of something. Not enough to matter. Enough to have done it.
You take one of something between you and eat half each, standing in a field that belongs to a stranger.
incidents: A tractor starts up two fields away and settles into a rhythm.
The crop moves against the wind in one narrow line, coming towards you.

Fields.label: Open Fields
Fields.intro:
Open country with the grass up and nothing in it taller than the two of you.
The sky is doing most of the work here.
question: Nothing has happened here. Ever. To anyone. Do you know how rare that is?
So? What do you make of it?
romantic: She lies back in the grass so only the sky can see her, and moves over to leave room.
No temples out here. No courtrooms. Nothing that wants a ruling out of me.
Down here I am about your size. Do not get used to it.
Fields.chaotic: The grass lies flat in a wide circle around the two of you and stays that way, politely, waiting to be explained.
activity: Walk out to the middle with me, where it is the same distance to everywhere.
You walk out until the edges of the field are all equally far away and stand in the only place that qualifies.
incidents: A hare gets up out of the grass much closer than either of you expected.
The wind crosses the whole field in one visible line and passes right through you.

Forest.label: Forest
Forest.intro:
Deep forest with the canopy closed over.
The light comes down in pieces and the ground eats every sound you make.
question: Every tree here is in a slow fight with every other tree. Centuries of it.
Nobody would find us in here. Is that a nice thought or not?
romantic: She stops in a shaft of light coming through the canopy and stands in it as though it were arranged.
This took a hundred and forty years to happen and it will last about nine minutes.
So come here. Do not make me say it again.
Forest.chaotic: Every tree in sight drops its leaves at once and grows them back green, and the wood is now a different season.
activity: Walk until we cannot see where we came in. Then a bit further.
You walk in until the way back is a guess. She looks pleased with the two of you.
incidents: Something heavy moves once in the undergrowth and then commits to being still.
A branch comes down somewhere behind you with the whole forest's attention on it.

ForestIce.label: Frozen Forest
ForestIce.intro:
A forest under hard frost. Every branch is furred with white and holding it.
The cold has taken the smell out of the air entirely.
question: Every one of these trees is asleep and doing it on purpose. They will all be back in April. Call that strategy.
Have you ever been somewhere this quiet on purpose?
romantic: She knocks the frost off a branch and it comes down over both of you like something arranged in advance.
The whole wood is waiting out a bad six months. It knows exactly how long to wait.
I have never known how long to wait for anything.
ForestIce.chaotic: Every tree in the wood sheds its frost in the same instant, and the whole forest is briefly a white cloud.
activity: Walk with me and do not knock anything off. Nobody has managed it yet.
You get about ninety metres before one of you ruins it, and neither of you will admit which.
incidents: A branch gives up its load with a sound like a very small building falling.
Tracks cross the path in front of you, fresh, and go nowhere in either direction.

ForestTropical.label: Tropical Forest
ForestTropical.intro:
Warm forest, three storeys of it, wet air and everything competing at once.
Something is calling and something else is answering it.
question: More things live in this square kilometre than in most countries. All of them are busy.
Does all this noise bother you? It is the sound of nobody caring we are here.
romantic: She stops under a leaf the size of a door and the rain that starts up does not reach either of you.
Nothing here is trying to impress anyone. It is all just trying.
I have spent four thousand years trying to impress people. Look how that went.
ForestTropical.chaotic: Every animal in earshot makes its call at the same instant. Then absolute silence, which is worse.
activity: Stand still and count the different things making noise. I bet you nine.
You count. It is thirty-one, and she pays up in a currency that does not exist.
incidents: Water comes off the canopy all at once as though something up there shifted its weight.
Something bright crosses in front of you at speed and neither of you identifies it.

Graveyard.label: Graveyard
Graveyard.intro:
A graveyard with the gate left open.
Everybody here has a date on them and nobody has an argument left.
question: Two dates and a dash. The dash is the part nobody can afford to carve.
Is this in bad taste? I genuinely cannot tell any more.
romantic: She sits with her back against a headstone belonging to somebody with a very long name.
Not one of them is frightened of me. It is the most restful company I get.
You are not frightened of me either. That is the part I keep checking.
Graveyard.chaotic: Every date on every stone in the yard reads the same for four seconds. It is today.
activity: Find me the oldest one that still has flowers. Somebody is still turning up for somebody.
You find it: a hundred and nine years old, and fresh flowers on it. Neither of you says anything for a while.
incidents: A vase blows over two rows away and rolls in a slow half circle.
A bird lands on a headstone, considers Eris, and stays.

Heaven.label: The Heavens
Heaven.intro:
Somewhere upstairs. Light with no source and architecture with no load.
Everything is in a good mood and it is not contagious.
question: I am not banned from up here. I want that established before anyone tells you otherwise.
Does it feel like anything to you? Genuinely. I have stopped being able to tell.
romantic: She sits on the edge of something that has no edge, and the light politely stops flattering her.
Everything here is finished. That is what makes it unbearable after the first century.
You are extremely unfinished. It is the best thing in this entire district.
Heaven.chaotic: Every note being held anywhere up here goes a semitone flat at once, and the effect is theological.
activity: Sit somewhere we are obviously not meant to sit and let us see how long it takes.
You sit somewhere improper. Nothing happens for a long time, which she takes as a victory.
incidents: Something enormous and courteous passes overhead and does not acknowledge either of you.
The light gets fractionally warmer, which she reads as being asked to leave.

Hell.label: The Inferno
Hell.intro:
Downstairs. It is warm, well organised, and much more administrative than the stories suggest.
Someone here has a filing system.
question: Everyone expects screaming. It is mostly paperwork. The screaming is a department.
Would you like to know if you are in the files? I can look. I should not.
romantic: She finds a ledge with a view over the whole works and sits with her back to it, facing you.
Everybody down there is being punished for exactly one thing. Consistency. It is almost kind.
Nobody has ever been able to tell me which of my things counts as the one.
Hell.chaotic: Every furnace in view changes colour, and the whole administration takes fourteen seconds to file the incident.
activity: Read the notices with me. The bureaucracy down here is the funniest writing in creation.
You read the noticeboards together. One of them is about her, and she does not let you finish it.
incidents: A queue somewhere below shuffles forward one place and settles.
Something in a uniform looks up at the two of you and decides it is above its pay grade.

Highlands.label: Highlands
Highlands.intro:
High rough country, all wind and low cloud and grass that has learned to lie down.
The weather here arrives before you can see it coming.
question: There is nothing between us and the next weather system. I find that clarifying.
Are you enjoying this, or are you being polite about a hill?
romantic: The cloud comes down and takes the view away, and the world is briefly this much across.
There. Now there is nothing else to look at and you cannot pretend there is.
I did not do that, before you ask. The weather did it and I will be taking the credit.
Highlands.chaotic: The cloud lifts off the whole range at once, in one piece, and hangs about a hundred metres up looking uncertain.
activity: Get to that cairn before the rain does. I am not helping you.
You both reach it and you both lose to the rain, and she is delighted about the whole business.
incidents: The wind changes direction completely and takes a moment to commit.
A sheep watches you both with an expression that she takes personally.

Highway.label: Highway
Highway.intro:
The verge of a motorway, at the hour when the traffic thins.
Everybody going past is going somewhere, at speed, without you.
question: Every one of those is somebody's whole life, doing ninety, for four seconds.
Would you get in one? If it stopped. Would you?
romantic: She sits on the barrier facing the traffic and lets the headlights go across her face one at a time.
Nobody out there will ever think about this evening. There is a freedom in being that unimportant.
I have never once been unimportant. Tonight I am trying it.
Highway.chaotic: Every vehicle on the carriageway changes lane at the same moment. Nobody crashes, which is somehow worse.
activity: Count the red ones with me. Loser has to wave at a lorry.
You both lose count almost immediately and she waves at a lorry anyway. It answers with the horn.
incidents: A car slows on the hard shoulder, thinks better of it, and rejoins.
The traffic stops entirely for nine seconds and then resumes with no explanation.

Houses.label: Residential Street
Houses.intro:
A street of houses with their evenings on behind the curtains.
Every window is a different programme.
question: Forty households, forty completely separate universes, all sharing a drainage system.
Which one would you want to be in? Do not say none of them.
romantic: She stops on the pavement and looks into a lit front room where somebody is doing nothing at all.
That. Whatever that is. Sitting in a room being unremarkable at each other.
Four thousand years and no one has ever offered me an evening like that.
Houses.chaotic: Every television on the street switches to the same channel, which is not broadcasting tonight.
activity: Walk the whole street with me and pick which house we would have ruined.
You walk the street picking houses. You choose the same one, which neither of you brings up again.
incidents: A security light comes on and follows you two houses along.
Somebody's dinner is audible through an open window and it is going badly.

HousesInside.label: Somebody's Home
HousesInside.intro:
Inside somebody's house. Their furniture, their smell, their entire way of arranging a room.
The heating is on for people who are not here.
question: Look at how they have done it. Somebody chose all of this in a shop.
Is it worse that we are in here, or that it is comfortable?
romantic: She sits down on somebody else's sofa in the way you only sit on your own.
This is what I do not have. Not the sofa. The having a sofa.
Do not say anything kind, I will be unbearable about it later.
HousesInside.chaotic: Every object in the house moves exactly ten centimetres to the left. The owners will feel it for years.
activity: Make me a cup of something in a stranger's kitchen. It is the most intimate crime there is.
You find the cups on the second attempt. She drinks it, and washes up, which is the strangest part.
incidents: The boiler fires up in another room and you both react as if caught.
A photograph on the shelf has been turned face down by whoever lives here.

Ice.label: Ice Flats
Ice.intro:
A flat sheet of ice going out to the edge of what you can see.
Every sound crosses it whole and arrives late.
question: Solid water. It is water lying about what it is and everyone lets it.
Is it safe? Do not check. Answer as though you knew.
romantic: She lies down flat on the ice and looks straight down through it.
There is a whole winter's worth of things frozen in here, all keeping.
Lie down. You have got to see this and I am not describing it to you.
Ice.chaotic: A crack runs from horizon to horizon under your feet, at speed, and does nothing else.
activity: Slide. Do not walk. Nobody has ever regretted sliding.
You slide out across the ice together and neither of you is good at it, which is the entire point.
incidents: The ice makes a noise like a long note bent out of tune and you feel it through your boots.
A bubble under the surface moves several metres to the left and stops.

Jungle.label: Jungle
Jungle.intro:
Jungle thick enough that the way you came in has already closed.
The heat is a physical opinion.
question: This place grows over anything you put in it. Roads. Cities. Gods.
How long do you think we would last if we sat down?
romantic: She pulls a curtain of green aside, holds it, and waits for you to go through first.
There are cities under this. Whole ones. Nobody remembers who was king.
Being forgotten does not frighten me. Being forgotten while still here does.
Jungle.chaotic: Everything green in view grows twice as fast for a full minute and the path behind you is gone for good.
activity: Find me something that was made by people. It is in here somewhere, everything is.
You find a worked stone under two centuries of root. She refuses to say whether she knew it was there.
incidents: Everything goes quiet in a circle around you and comes back in from the outside.
Something drops out of the canopy behind you, lands wetly, and is not investigated.

Laboratory.label: Laboratory
Laboratory.intro:
A laboratory with the work left out mid-experiment.
Something on a bench is at a stage that cannot be paused, and has been.
question: Somebody is trying to find something out. That is the whole species in one room.
Would you want to know how everything works, if it cost you the liking of it?
romantic: She looks down a microscope somebody left focused, and does not say what is on the slide.
Whoever set this up will come back tomorrow and be wrong about it. That is the job.
Being wrong on purpose, over and over, for years. It is the bravest thing you people do.
Laboratory.chaotic: Every experiment in the room completes at once, successfully, with results that contradict each other.
activity: Write something in the logbook. Something true. They will never work out who.
You leave one true line in a stranger's logbook. She reads it twice and does not add one of her own.
incidents: A centrifuge somewhere finishes its run and beeps until it is ignored.
Something in a sealed jar has moved since you came in.

Lair.label: Lair
Lair.intro:
A lair: a place something large has made comfortable for itself.
The scale of everything is wrong for people.
question: Whatever lives here is not small and it is not out.
Shall we wait for it, or is that just me?
romantic: She sits down on a hoard that belongs to something else and does not touch any of it.
It is not the gold. It never is. It is having one place nothing else is allowed into.
You are allowed in. That is the whole announcement, I am not doing a speech.
Lair.chaotic: Everything in the hoard rearranges into a neat spiral, largest at the outside, in complete silence.
activity: Put something into the hoard instead of taking. I want to see if it notices.
You add one worthless object to the pile. Something deep in the lair goes very still.
incidents: Air moves through the lair in one long breath and comes back.
Something enormous shifts its weight far enough away not to matter yet.

Lake.label: Lakeside
Lake.intro:
A lake with the evening on it, flat enough to be embarrassing.
The far shore is doing the same thing back at you.
question: Look at it holding the whole sky and not spilling any of it.
Skimming stones. Yes or no. This decides several things.
romantic: She sits at the water's edge with her feet in, and the whole surface stops moving to accommodate her.
A lake keeps everything that goes into it. It has no outlet and no opinion.
Tell me something you have not told anyone. It will keep that too.
Lake.chaotic: The lake rings from the middle outwards, six perfect circles, none of them caused by anything.
activity: Skim one. If you get more than four I will be insufferable about having brought you.
You both skim badly for twenty minutes. Her best is three and she blames the lake.
incidents: A fish takes something off the surface out in the middle and the rings take a long time to arrive.
The far shore goes out of focus, comes back, and is slightly closer.

Landfill.label: Landfill
Landfill.intro:
A landfill, layered and steaming gently.
Everything anybody ever decided against is here in one place.
question: This is the most honest museum in the country and nobody has curated a thing.
Is it awful? It is awful. Do you want to leave?
romantic: She climbs to the top of the tip and sits down on it as though it were a hill, which it now is.
Everything up here was wanted once. Every single item. That is what gets me.
Discarded is not the same as worthless. I have needed that to be true for a long time.
Landfill.chaotic: Everything in the landfill sorts itself by the year it was thrown away, in strata, visibly, in under a minute.
activity: Find the best thing here. There is always one and somebody was an idiot to bin it.
You find a perfectly good chair. She sits in it, on top of the tip, like a magistrate.
incidents: Gulls come up off the tip all at once for no reason either of you can find.
Something under the surface settles and a slow breath of warm air comes out.

Limbo.label: Limbo
Limbo.intro:
Nowhere in particular, and it is fully committed to that.
There is a horizon but nothing has agreed to be on it.
question: This is where things go that were never decided about. It is enormous.
Do you find waiting restful, or is it the worst thing there is?
romantic: There is nothing to sit on, so she simply stops, and the two of you are the only event in the place.
Everything here is still pending. Nobody has ruled on any of it.
I rule on things for a living now. In here I am off duty and it is terrifying.
Limbo.chaotic: Something almost happens. It gets extremely close, four times, and then does not.
activity: Decide something. Anything. Out loud. It has to count for something in here.
You say a small decision out loud. The place takes it seriously in a way that is hard to shake off.
incidents: A distance changes without anything having moved.
You both realise you have stopped being able to say how long you have been here.

LootCellar.label: Cellar
LootCellar.intro:
A small cellar somebody meant to come back for.
There is more in here than the room admits to.
question: Somebody hid all this and then had a worse week than they planned.
Do you take things that are not yours? Be honest, I will know.
romantic: It is a small room and neither of you makes an effort to use all of it.
I have been in treasuries with a ceiling you cannot see. They were worse than this.
Everything valuable I have ever been given was an attempt to make me leave.
LootCellar.chaotic: Everything in the cellar rearranges itself by value, most precious at the front, in under two seconds.
activity: Open one thing. Your choice. I will not look until you have decided.
You open one crate between you. What is in it is worth less than the wait was.
incidents: Something settles on a shelf with the sound of a coin choosing a side.
The door at the top of the steps moves, and does not open.

Mangrove.label: Mangroves
Mangrove.intro:
Mangroves: trees standing in the sea on their own roots, refusing to pick a side.
The water goes in and out of the whole wood twice a day.
question: Not land, not sea. They just refused to choose and got away with it.
Have you ever refused to choose? How did that go for you?
romantic: She balances along a root above the water and does not offer you a hand. Trust, of a sort.
These hold an entire coastline together by refusing to be one thing.
I have been three things this century and none of them held anything together.
Mangrove.chaotic: The tide comes in and goes out through the whole mangrove in forty seconds, and everything living panics on schedule.
activity: Walk the roots with me. Whoever gets wet first buys.
You both get wet within a minute, at the same moment, which settles nothing.
incidents: Something small and armoured crosses a root in front of you and does not hurry.
The water level drops enough to hear it happening.

Meadows.label: Meadow
Meadows.intro:
A meadow in flower, loud with insects doing their entire year's work.
The air is thick and sweet and slightly too much.
question: Every one of these flowers is a bribe. That is all a flower is.
Would it work on you? The bribe, I mean.
romantic: She picks nothing, which for a goddess in a flower meadow is a considerable act of restraint.
If I pick one it dies for a compliment. That is a bad trade and I have made it before.
They can all stay where they are. I have got somewhere to be.
Meadows.chaotic: Every flower in the meadow turns to face the two of you, and then closes, and then opens again as something else.
activity: Find me the ugliest flower in this meadow. There is always one and it is always trying.
You find it together. It is genuinely awful and she carries it for the rest of the evening.
incidents: A bee makes a serious attempt at her hair and is talked out of it.
The insect noise stops all at once for two seconds and then resumes.

Metro.label: Metro
Metro.intro:
An underground station between trains. Tiled, lit too well, and completely empty.
Air moves through the tunnel from a train that has not arrived.
question: Half a million people a day and right now it is ours. I checked the timetable.
Where would you go, if the next one went anywhere?
romantic: She sits on a platform bench and the departure board over her head clears itself of destinations.
Nothing is coming for eleven minutes. I have checked. I have checked twice.
Eleven minutes is the longest I have ever booked for anybody.
Metro.chaotic: Every departure board in the station shows the same destination, which no line serves and nobody has heard of.
activity: Sit on the platform with me and let one go past without getting on it.
A train comes, opens, waits, and leaves without either of you. The station is very quiet afterwards.
incidents: The tunnel breathes out warm air ahead of nothing at all.
An announcement plays in a language that is not one of the ones on the signs.

Mines.label: Mines
Mines.intro:
Worked mine galleries, timbered and abandoned by the shift.
Everything here was carried out by hand, upwards.
question: Every metre of this was somebody's whole working life. Metre by metre.
Would you go down here every morning for thirty years?
romantic: She puts her hand on a timber prop and looks up at the weight it is holding.
One piece of wood, one hundred and forty years, all of that above it. Nobody ever thanks the prop.
I am not the prop in anybody's life. I have always been the weight.
Mines.chaotic: Every lamp in the workings lights at once, all the way down, and you can see how far it actually goes.
activity: Go down one more level with me. Just one. Then we will be sensible.
You go down one more level, and then another, and the sensible part never arrives.
incidents: A prop takes up some slack somewhere and the sound travels the whole gallery.
Somebody's initials are cut into the rock at eye height, dated.

Mountain.label: Mountainside
Mountain.intro:
High on a mountainside, above the last of the trees.
The air is thin and everything below is a map of itself.
question: People put their gods on mountains because they could not be bothered to climb them.
You climbed one. What did you expect to find at the top?
romantic: She sits on a rock with the whole country laid out beneath her and turns her back on all of it.
I have had altars on peaks like this. The view is the same and nobody was ever up here.
You came up here. On foot. Knowing what I am.
Mountain.chaotic: The whole range echoes back a sound that neither of you made, and it takes its time about it.
activity: Build a cairn with me. Three stones. It is how you tell the next person somebody was here.
You build a small pile of stones on the ridge. It will outlast both the evening and one of you.
incidents: A cloud arrives at your height and passes through the two of you.
Something makes a noise a very long way below and it reaches you late.

MountainDesert.label: Desert Highlands
MountainDesert.intro:
Dry mountains with no forgiveness in them. Rock, thin air, and a long way down on two sides.
The wind up here has come a very long way.
question: High and dry. Nothing lives here that has not made a serious commitment.
Are you out of breath, or is that me?
romantic: She sits on the edge with her legs over the drop and does not hold on to anything.
Everything down there is having a completely different evening.
Sit. I will catch you. Probably. It would be a good story either way.
MountainDesert.chaotic: A rockfall starts on the opposite face and stops halfway down, holding its position, waiting.
activity: Climb the last bit with me. I want to see everything at once for a minute.
You take the last of the ridge together and stand where the wind will not let you talk.
incidents: A stone you did not kick goes over the edge behind you.
A bird holds absolutely still in the wind at eye level for four seconds.

MountainIce.label: Frozen Peak
MountainIce.intro:
A peak above the snow line, in wind that does not stop for anyone.
Every breath costs something.
question: Nothing lives up here. Nothing has ever lived up here. It is wonderfully rude.
Are you cold? You can say yes. I will not think less of you, I will just enjoy it.
romantic: She stands in the full wind on the summit and lets it take her hair and her coat and her composure.
Nothing up here is pretending. The mountain would kill us both and not even be doing it on purpose.
I have been meant on purpose by everything for four thousand years. This is a holiday.
MountainIce.chaotic: The wind stops. Entirely. On a summit. For eight seconds. Then it comes back from the other direction.
activity: Stand on the actual top with me. Both feet. It only fits one person.
You share the summit badly, holding on to each other because the alternative is worse.
incidents: A plume of snow comes off the ridge above and goes horizontally for two hundred metres.
The cloud below opens and you can see a single village, lit, very far down.

Mushroom.label: Fungal Wood
Mushroom.intro:
A wood of fungus grown to the size of trees, and glowing where it feels like it.
The air tastes of spores and something older.
question: Underneath all this is one organism. One. This entire wood is somebody having a thought.
Does that unsettle you? It should, a bit.
romantic: The glow comes up brighter where she stands, follows her three steps, and then follows you instead.
It has decided about you. I have no say in it and I want that noted.
It has excellent judgement, which is annoying of it.
Mushroom.chaotic: Every cap in the wood releases at once, and for a moment you are standing inside a slow gold snowstorm.
activity: Touch one and see what the rest of the wood does about it.
You touch one cap. Three hundred metres away, in sequence, the whole wood answers.
incidents: A patch of glow travels past under the ground, going somewhere with purpose.
Spores land on her shoulder and stay lit for a while.

Ocean.label: Open Sea
Ocean.intro:
Open water with no land in any direction.
The swell moves underneath you like something breathing in its sleep.
question: Nobody owns this. Every treaty on it is a piece of paper on top of nothing.
Do you know how deep it is here? Neither do I, and I have looked.
romantic: She looks over the side at water going down further than the light does and does not say anything for a while.
The sea has never once needed a name to be enormous. I have envied that my whole existence.
Say my name anyway. Out here it will not go anywhere.
Ocean.chaotic: The swell turns square. For thirty seconds the whole ocean is a grid, and then it is embarrassed and stops.
activity: Look for land. There is not any. I want to watch you look.
You go all the way round the horizon. Nothing, in every direction, and neither of you minds it.
incidents: Something breaks the surface a long way off and is gone before you can point.
The swell changes direction under you without the wind changing at all.

Office.label: Office
Office.intro:
An office floor after hours. Screens asleep, chairs left at the angle their people left them.
A printer somewhere is still ready.
question: Everyone here spent a third of their life at that desk and left it exactly like that.
Which desk would be yours? You have already picked one, I can tell.
romantic: She sits on the edge of a desk that is not hers, in a building that is not hers, at an hour that is.
Look at the photographs. Every single desk has somebody else's face on it.
Nobody has ever put me on a desk. It would be a strange thing to want and I want it.
Office.chaotic: Every screen on the floor wakes at once and displays the same document, which is a resignation letter.
activity: Sit in the best chair on this floor with me. There is always one and everyone knows which.
You find it in the corner office. You take turns in it and neither of you is impressed.
incidents: The printer takes a sheet, prints nothing on it, and delivers it.
A phone rings twice on an empty desk and gives up.

OmegaTower.label: Omega Tower
OmegaTower.intro:
The ground at the foot of the Omega Tower, which goes up past the point where looking helps.
Everything nearby leans very slightly towards it.
opening: You picked here. Of all the places on this world, you picked here.
Mortals call it the Omega Tower now.
But I remember when it was something else...
question: This tower... has an interesting history.
During the Y2K event, when chaos reigned supreme...
I challenged Ma'at, the Egyptian goddess of justice, to a divine duel.
Her spear... well, let's say I won.
And when a goddess falls, her tools remain.
That spear embedded itself in the earth, growing, transforming.
Now it's become the lynchpin of the multiverse itself.
Ironic, isn't it? A tool of justice keeping reality stable.
Sometimes I think about what would happen if I removed it...
But then, without a universe, who would be left to believe in me?
And without believers... even we gods fade away.
Thousands of forgotten gods know that too well.
choices: You took her place as goddess of justice?
Aren't you afraid of fading away?
That tower is beautiful and terrifying
romantic: She puts a hand flat against the base of the tower, the way you would touch something you had put down.
Everything holding together up there is holding together because I won an argument.
I have never once been able to say that about anything smaller.
OmegaTower.chaotic: The whole tower rings once, from the ground to wherever it stops, and several distant things go briefly wrong.
activity: Walk round the base with me. Nobody ever does, they all just look up.
You walk the entire circumference. It takes longer than either of you expected and she counts every step.
incidents: A shadow crosses the ground that has no business belonging to anything on it.
For a moment the tower is a spear, and then it is a tower again, and she does not comment.

Park.label: Park
Park.intro:
A city park with the gates about to be locked.
Somebody has designed nature here and been slightly too pleased about it.
question: Every tree in here is where a committee put it. And it works. That is the offensive part.
Benches, ducks and a bandstand. Is this a date or a diorama?
romantic: She sits at one end of a bench and puts her arm along the back of it, which is not subtle.
This is where mortals do it. Benches. Four thousand years and it is still benches.
So sit on the bench. I am not going to explain it twice.
Park.chaotic: Every flowerbed in the park comes into bloom out of season, in the wrong colours, in a wave from the gates inwards.
activity: Feed the ducks with me. I want to see who they go for.
The ducks go for her, en masse, immediately, and she is completely undone by it.
incidents: A keeper rattles the gates at the far end and shouts a time at nobody.
A sprinkler comes on for eleven seconds and thinks better of it.

PatronVault.label: The Vault
PatronVault.intro:
A vault built on a scale nobody needed, for one person's things.
Every footstep in here comes back off six walls.
question: Somebody owns all of this and is not here. That is the most decadent thing in the room.
What would you keep, if you could keep anything?
romantic: She walks the length of the great hall and stops in the middle, where all of it is equally far away.
Every single thing in here is owned. That is the only fact about any of it.
You are the only thing standing in this room that belongs to itself.
PatronVault.chaotic: Every strongroom door in the vault unlocks at once, and the sound of it goes on for a while.
activity: Shout something. I want to know how big this actually is.
You measure the vault by shouting into it. It is bigger than either of you was prepared for.
incidents: A coin comes off a pile somewhere and takes an unreasonable time to stop rolling.
A light you did not light is on in the back chamber.

Permafrost.label: Permafrost
Permafrost.intro:
Frozen ground that has been frozen since before anyone was counting.
Everything that ever fell here is still here, at the depth it stopped.
question: Nothing rots here. Everything that died is still exactly as annoyed as it was.
Would you want to be kept, or would you rather go?
romantic: She crouches and puts her hand flat on ground that has not been warm since before her name existed.
Under here there are flowers from an age nobody wrote down. Still the right colour.
Things keep, if nothing warm gets to them. I have been testing that theory for a while.
Permafrost.chaotic: Four thousand years of frozen ground thaws to a depth of one metre and freezes again, and something down there is briefly awake.
activity: Dig. Not far. Whatever we find has been waiting a very long time for company.
You get down about a foot and find a leaf, perfectly green, from a summer nobody remembers.
incidents: The ground gives a single dull crack somewhere under both of you.
Mist comes up out of the ground in a straight line and stays there.

River.label: River
River.intro:
A river going past at its own pace, ignoring both of you completely.
It is louder than it looks and colder than it sounds.
question: All of this is leaving. Constantly. And it looks like it is staying.
Everything you drop in it is somebody else's problem by morning. Tempting, no?
romantic: She puts a hand into the current, holds it there against the pull, and looks at you the entire time.
You cannot stand in the same one twice. Somebody clever said that and then went home.
So this is the only version of this evening there is going to be. Behave accordingly.
River.chaotic: The river runs backwards. Not fast, not violently: it simply reverses, politely, for about a minute.
activity: Race something down it with me. Two sticks. Loser admits something.
You race two sticks under the bank. Hers loses, and she admits something small and true.
incidents: Something goes past in the current that was clearly indoors this morning.
The water level comes up a hand's width and stays there.

RiverBank.label: Riverbank
RiverBank.intro:
The soft ground beside a river, cut and rebuilt by every flood there has ever been.
Everything here grows fast and gets taken away regularly.
question: This bank is in a different place every decade and the map has never once been updated.
Do you like things that move under you?
romantic: She sits down where the bank is undercut and lets her feet hang over moving water.
This whole edge will be gone in thirty years. Somebody will be standing in the river here.
I like knowing the exact expiry date of somewhere I am happy.
RiverBank.chaotic: The bank rebuilds itself: three metres of new ground unrolls into the river and holds, complete with grass.
activity: Look for something the water left. There is always something and it is always strange.
You find a bone, a bottle and a key. She keeps the key and will not discuss it.
incidents: A piece of the bank goes into the water further down with a soft, final sound.
Something with a burrow decides you are both fine and goes back to work.

Road.label: The Road
Road.intro:
A road going both ways, with nobody on it in either direction.
Somebody surveyed this line, once, and everyone has agreed with them since.
question: Roads are the only honest architecture. They only exist to be somewhere else from.
Which way would you have gone, if I had not turned up?
romantic: She stands on the centre line, where nobody is supposed to stand, and there is nothing coming.
Everybody on a road is on their way to somebody. That is all a road is for.
I have never been the destination. Not once, in four thousand years.
Road.chaotic: The road's markings peel up off the surface, rearrange, and lay themselves back down pointing somewhere else entirely.
activity: Walk down the middle with me until something makes us move.
You walk the centre line for a mile. Nothing comes, and by the end neither of you wants anything to.
incidents: A single vehicle passes, slows for no reason, and speeds up again.
A signpost points at a place neither of you has ever heard of.

Ruins.label: Ruins
Ruins.intro:
Ruins with enough left standing to tell you what it was.
Somebody's very good idea, eight hundred years after the last person agreed with it.
question: Everything gets to this eventually. Every wall, every empire, every one of us.
Does it depress you, or is that just good taste?
romantic: She sits in a doorway that has no building attached to it any more, framed by nothing.
This was somebody's front door. They came through it every day for forty years.
