Nothing outlasts being loved daily. Not marble. I have checked.
Ruins.chaotic: Every fallen stone in the ruin lifts a foot off the ground, holds, and settles back into a slightly better building.
activity: Rebuild one wall with me. Badly. It is the thought that counts and the thought is spite.
You stack fallen stones into two courses of a wall. It will be the newest thing here for another century.
incidents: A stone comes off a wall on its own and lands where it was always going to.
You find a carved face that is still, unmistakably, laughing at somebody.

SaltFlats.label: Salt Flats
SaltFlats.intro:
A salt pan flat enough to see the curve of the world on.
There is a film of water on it and the sky has fallen over.
question: There are two skies and no ground. Nobody built this and nobody can improve it.
Say something true out here. It is the only place I trust an answer.
romantic: She walks out onto the film of water until she is standing in the sky, and turns round.
There is nothing here to hide behind. No pillars, no crowd, no weather.
So I am going to be straightforward for a minute and you are going to let me.
SaltFlats.chaotic: The reflection stops copying the sky and starts showing a completely different one, with the wrong number of moons.
activity: Walk out until neither of us can tell which way up we are.
You walk out into the middle of the reflected sky and stand there being the only vertical thing for miles.
incidents: Your own reflection is a half second behind you, once, and then catches up.
A wind crosses the whole pan and every reflection tilts together.

Savannah.label: Savannah
Savannah.intro:
Grass to the horizon with a few trees standing about like witnesses.
Everything out here can see everything else coming.
question: Nothing here can hide. Everything just watches everything else and agrees to wait.
Would you be predator or prey? Do not think about it, just say.
romantic: She sits with her back to one of the lone trees and the whole plain arranges itself in front of you.
This is the shape of country your species stood up in. You are homesick and you do not know it.
I have no shape of country. I have wherever the argument is.
Savannah.chaotic: Every animal on the plain looks up at the same instant, at the same thing, which is not there.
activity: Watch that tree line with me until something comes out of it.
Something does, eventually, and it is enormous and unhurried and does not care about either of you.
incidents: Dust comes up on the horizon and settles again without resolving into anything.
The grass moves against the wind in one line for about two hundred metres.

SeaBed.label: Sea Floor
SeaBed.intro:
The floor of the sea, with the whole weight of it overhead.
The light that reaches down here has had most of itself taken off it.
question: Everything above us is water and everything below us is older than water.
Nothing down here has ever needed to look good. It is very restful.
romantic: She walks along the bottom slowly because there is no other speed available, and everything she stirs up takes an age to settle.
Nothing here has ever heard a rumour. There is no gossip at this depth.
Do you know how long it is since I was somewhere nobody had an opinion about me?
SeaBed.chaotic: Every light-making thing on the bottom switches on at once, and for a few seconds the sea floor is a city.
activity: Pick something up off the bottom. Whatever it is, it has been there longer than your language.
You pick up something worked by hands. Neither of you says what you think it was.
incidents: Something goes over the two of you, blocking what light there was, and takes a while to finish going over.
The silt you disturbed twenty seconds ago is still coming down.

Sewer.label: Sewers
Sewer.intro:
A brick sewer, vaulted like a chapel by somebody who took it seriously.
Everything the city has decided against is going past your feet.
question: Look at that vaulting. Somebody made this beautiful and no one was ever going to see it.
That is the purest work there is. Do you agree, or are you being sick?
romantic: She holds a light up to the brickwork and finds a date and a mason's mark from a hundred and sixty years ago.
He signed it. Down here. Where nobody would ever look.
That is what I want. Not the temples. That.
Sewer.chaotic: Every outfall in the system runs clear water for one minute, which will cause four separate official inquiries.
activity: Find another mark. There will be more of them and I want the whole set.
You find six between you. Two are the same man, twenty years apart, in different tunnels.
incidents: The water level rises and falls a hand's width for no reason you can see.
Something splashes ahead of you and does not splash again.

Snow.label: Snowfield
Snow.intro:
Open ground under fresh snow, still coming down.
Every sound in the world has had a blanket put over it.
question: Nothing has crossed this yet. In about four minutes that will have stopped being true.
Do you want the first footprints, or shall I?
romantic: She catches a flake on the back of her hand and stops it there, unmelted, for as long as she can be bothered.
There are eleven trillion of these coming down tonight and no two are the same. It sounds like poetry. It is arithmetic.
Every one of them is going to be water by morning anyway. So is this. So look at it.
Snow.chaotic: The snow stops. Not on the ground: in the air. Every flake in sight holds its position for six seconds.
activity: Fall over backwards with me. On purpose. In the snow. Now.
You both go over backwards into it and lie there, and the snow keeps coming down onto your faces.
incidents: The snow comes down heavier for about a minute, as though something was decided.
A set of prints crosses yours that neither of you saw being made.

Space.label: Open Space
Space.intro:
Vacuum, with everything in it very far away and very old.
There is no up here and both of you have quietly picked one anyway.
question: Everything you can see is a photograph of something that has already stopped doing that.
Does the scale of it frighten you? Answer honestly, it frightens me.
romantic: With nothing to stand on she simply turns to face you, and there is nothing else in any direction.
Gods are supposed to be comfortable out here. I have never once been.
You are the nearest thing to a horizon I have got. Stay put.
Space.chaotic: Every star in view goes out for one full second. Nothing else happens, and she does not apologise.
activity: Pick a star. We are going to decide what is happening there right now.
You pick one and invent a civilisation for it. Hers has a very detailed and vindictive legal system.
incidents: Something crosses in front of a distant star and takes four minutes to finish crossing.
You both notice at the same time that it has been silent this whole while.

Spacecenter.label: Space Centre
Spacecenter.intro:
A launch complex between missions. Gantries, hard standing, and a countdown clock stopped at a number.
Everything here was built by people who wanted to leave.
question: Your entire species looked up and then built the ladder. On the second attempt.
Would you go? If they asked tomorrow and it was one way?
romantic: She stands under the gantry looking straight up the way somebody looks at a thing they are jealous of.
Nobody prayed to get up there. They did arithmetic. Enormous quantities of arithmetic.
You did it without us. I have never been prouder of anything I had no part in.
Spacecenter.chaotic: Every clock on the complex resets to nine seconds and holds there, and somewhere an alarm is extremely polite about it.
activity: Read the plaques with me. They put every name on. Every single one.
You read the names off the wall. It takes a long time, and she does not skip any.
incidents: A vent releases somewhere on the pad and the whole complex ticks as it cools.
A light on a control tower changes colour and nobody comes.

SpiritWoods.label: Spirit Woods
SpiritWoods.intro:
A wood with too many things standing in it that are not trees.
None of them are hostile and all of them have noticed you.
question: Every one of these was something once. Most of them cannot remember what.
That is what happens when you are stopped believing in. Still want to be here?
romantic: The shapes between the trees move back a respectful distance, all at once, without being asked.
They know what I am. None of them respect me. They are being professionally polite.
One day I will be standing where they are. I would like somebody to have known me first.
SpiritWoods.chaotic: Every spirit in the wood turns to face the same direction, which is not towards either of you, and holds.
activity: Say hello to one. Out loud. Nobody has, in a very long time.
You greet one of them properly. It does not answer, but the whole wood is warmer afterwards.
incidents: One of them comes closer than the others and stops just inside politeness.
A name is said somewhere behind you and neither of you asks whose it was.

Steppe.label: Steppe
Steppe.intro:
Grassland going on past the point where it means anything.
There is one road across it and you cannot see either end.
question: Every empire that ever crossed this decided it was empty. All of them were wrong and all of them are gone.
Could you live somewhere with no edges?
romantic: She sits down in the grass and the horizon is at the same height all the way round the two of you.
There is no landmark here. Nothing to arrange yourself against. You just have to pick a direction and believe it.
I have picked one. Do not make me say what it is.
Steppe.chaotic: The grass lays over in a spiral three hundred metres wide, centred exactly on the two of you.
activity: Walk to nothing in particular with me and see how long it takes to arrive.
You walk for an hour towards a point you both chose. It is exactly as far away as it was.
incidents: A horse without anybody on it watches from a distance and then is not there.
The wind carries the sound of a bell from somewhere that has no bell.

Swamp.label: Swamp
Swamp.intro:
Standing water and standing trees, and it is very hard to tell where either of them stops.
The ground is a rumour.
question: Nothing here has committed to being solid. I have been accused of the same thing.
Is this the worst place I could have brought you? Be honest.
romantic: She finds the one hummock that will take both your weights, and it does, barely.
Everything in a swamp is halfway through becoming something else. Nothing is finished.
I would rather be unfinished with you than settled with anyone.
Swamp.chaotic: Every bubble the swamp has been saving comes up at once and the whole place exhales for eleven seconds.
activity: Find the deepest bit without falling in it. That is the game, those are the rules.
You find it. One of you falls in it. Neither of you is willing to say it was them.
incidents: Something long moves under the surface, unhurried, and does not surface.
A light shows in the trees, at head height, and goes out when looked at directly.

Taiga.label: Taiga
Taiga.intro:
Conifers for as far as the road goes, all of them the same height and none of them interested.
The forest floor is dry needles and absolutely nothing else.
question: One species, four hundred kilometres. The most single-minded landscape there is.
Do you admire that, or does it worry you?
romantic: She stops walking, and the silence that arrives is so complete that neither of you starts again straight away.
Nothing lives on this floor. It is all up in the tops, out of the way, minding itself.
I am very good at being out of the way. It is not the same as being left alone.
Taiga.chaotic: Every tree in view drops its cones at once, and the sound goes through the forest like applause getting further away.
activity: Walk until the road is out of sight. Then listen. This place has a sound and you have to earn it.
You get far enough in for the silence to have a texture. Neither of you talks over it.
incidents: Something crosses the path fifty metres ahead, on four legs, without hurrying.
A tree cracks somewhere in the cold and the sound arrives from the wrong direction.

Temple.label: Temple Grounds
Temple.intro:
The grounds of a working temple, swept this morning by somebody who does it every morning.
Everything here is at the angle it was ordered to be.
question: Somebody swept this at dawn. They will do it again tomorrow. That is the entire religion.
Is that devotion or is it just a job? I have never been able to tell from this side.
romantic: She stands at the bottom of the steps and does not go up them, which for her is enormous.
I could walk in there. Nothing would stop me. That is the problem with all of it.
Out here I have to be invited. Go on, then.
Temple.chaotic: Every bell, chime and hanging thing on the grounds sounds at once, and the note holds much longer than it should.
activity: Do the thing properly with me. Whatever they do here. We are going to do it correctly.
You follow the local form exactly, both of you, without irony. It is the strangest thing she has done all year.
incidents: A bell is rung once inside and not explained.
Somebody crosses the yard, sees Eris, and completes their route at exactly the same pace.

TempleInside.label: Temple Interior
TempleInside.intro:
Inside a temple to somebody else. Offerings gone hard in their bowls, a floor worn concave by knees.
The room is built to make one figure look larger than you.
question: A competitor's premises again. I am starting to think you are doing this deliberately.
Whoever they were, they got a floor worn out by kneeling. What would you want?
romantic: She sits down on the steps of somebody else's altar with her back to it.
I know exactly how much of this was sincere. It is not the number you would guess.
Nobody has ever knelt for me and meant it. I would not know what to do with it.
TempleInside.chaotic: Every offering in the temple goes fresh again at once, and the smell of it is overwhelming and wrong.
activity: Leave something. Anything. I want to see whose name it goes under.
You leave a small worthless thing on the altar. Nothing happens, which she says is the correct response.
incidents: A bowl on the altar tips over on its own and rights itself.
The statue is not looking where it was looking when you came in.

TempleShinto.label: Shrine
TempleShinto.intro:
A shrine with a torii at the path and a rope on an old tree.
Everything here is looked after by somebody who is not showing off about it.
question: They put a rope round a tree and that made it somebody. I like that. It is very economical.
What would you put a rope round, if it worked?
romantic: She stops at the torii, waits, and only then walks through, off to one side of the middle.
The middle is for whoever lives here. You walk at the side. Everybody knows that and nobody enforces it.
An entire courtesy with no punishment attached. I would not have thought of it.
TempleShinto.chaotic: Every paper tied to the rack unties itself, rearranges, and reties. All the wishes are now somebody else's.
activity: Write one and tie it up. I want to see if you cheat and write something sensible.
You tie yours to the rack. She writes one too, folds it so it cannot be read, and ties it beside yours.
incidents: The rope on the old tree moves in a wind that has not reached the ground.
A cat crosses the gravel with the confidence of the resident deity.

Train.label: Station
Train.intro:
A railway station with the last services still listed.
Wind comes down the platform from an arrival that is running late.
question: Stations are the only buildings that are entirely about somewhere else.
Have you ever met anybody off a train? Properly, on the platform?
romantic: She stands at the end of the platform where the roof stops, and the last of the light is on her.
Everyone here is being met or not being met. There is no third category.
Nobody has ever stood on a platform for me. I have thought about it more than I would like.
Train.chaotic: Every departure on the board advances by one minute, at once, for ever, and the station accepts this immediately.
activity: Let's go up. Every station has a way onto the roof and every one of them is unlocked.
You get onto the station roof. The whole city is laid out below and there is nobody up here but the two of you.
incidents: An announcement apologises for something that has not happened yet.
A train goes straight through without slowing and takes all the paper on the platform with it.

Tundra.label: Tundra
Tundra.intro:
Low ground, low plants, and a sky doing nearly all of the work.
Nothing here grows above knee height because nothing here is allowed to.
question: Everything here is a hundred years old and eight centimetres tall. Think about that.
Slow and stubborn, or fast and finished? Which are you?
romantic: She kneels and shows you a plant the size of a coin that is older than the last four wars.
It survived by not being interesting. Nobody grazed it, nobody picked it, nobody wrote about it.
I have never once managed to be uninteresting. It is going to kill me eventually.
Tundra.chaotic: The whole tundra flowers at once, everything at ground level, out of season, in one silent second.
activity: Lie down. From down here it is a forest and we are the wrong size for it.
You lie down in a hundred-year-old forest eight centimetres tall and neither of you gets up for a while.
incidents: The light goes long and low without the sun appearing to have moved.
A bird calls once, a very long way off, and nothing answers it.

Underdark.label: The Underdark
Underdark.intro:
Deep places under the deep places, on a scale that was not made for anyone.
There is a horizon down here, which is the wrong thing for a cave to have.
question: There is weather down here. That is how big it is. Caves are not supposed to have weather.
Does knowing how much rock is above us help or is it worse?
romantic: She stops at the edge of a drop with a city's worth of dark on the far side of it.
Nothing down here has ever seen the sun and none of it is missing anything.
I keep being told what I ought to want. Down here nobody is telling anybody anything.
Underdark.chaotic: Every luminous thing in the whole cavern dims and brightens together, twice, like a very large animal blinking.
activity: Shout across it with me. I want to know if there is a far side.
You shout across the dark together. Something comes back and it is not either of your voices.
incidents: A stone you did not drop lands somewhere below and keeps going.
A light moves across the cavern very far off, at a steady pace, going somewhere.

Villa.label: Villa
Villa.intro:
A private villa with the grounds kept and nobody in residence.
Everything here was chosen to be seen by people who were invited.
question: Somebody spends a fortune a year on this and comes for three weeks in August.
Are we trespassing? We are. Does it improve it?
romantic: She sits on the edge of the empty fountain as though she had been asked to, at length, by letter.
Everything here is arranged for a guest who never quite arrives.
I have been the guest who never arrives for a very long time. Tonight I turned up.
Villa.chaotic: Every light in the villa comes on, the fountain starts, and music begins for a party that was cancelled in another decade.
activity: Use the good room. Sit on the furniture nobody is allowed to sit on.
You sit on the untouchable furniture in the best room in the house and nothing at all happens to you.
incidents: A shutter somewhere in the house is opened and closed by nobody.
The gardener's radio is still on, somewhere down the grounds, playing to the hedges.

Village.label: Village
Village.intro:
A village of thirty roofs with the evening meal happening behind all of them.
Somebody's dog has already told everyone you are here.
question: Thirty families and one argument that has been running since 1840.
Do you want to know what it is about? I can find out in four minutes.
romantic: She sits on the low wall by the well, where everybody in the village has sat at some point in their life.
Everyone here will be buried within a mile of where they were born. All of them. On purpose.
I have never been anywhere twice on purpose. Tonight is technically a start.
Village.chaotic: Every door in the village opens at the same moment, and thirty people look out at nothing, and go back in.
activity: Sit here until somebody comes out to find out who we are.
Somebody does. She tells them a name that is not hers and they accept it entirely.
incidents: A dog barks twice, is told off by name, and stops.
Somebody's window closes as you look at it, and the light behind it does not go off.

VillageDesert.label: Desert Village
VillageDesert.intro:
A village of thick walls and small windows, built entirely against the sun.
The streets are narrow on purpose and the shade is the town's main asset.
question: Every wall here is a metre thick. Nobody built that for the look of it. They were arguing with the sky.
Would you have stayed and built, or moved on?
romantic: She leads you down the shaded side of a street barely wide enough for the two of you.
They built the streets this narrow so people would have to pass close. It is deliberate.
Four thousand years of divine architecture and nobody thought of that.
VillageDesert.chaotic: Every water jar in the village fills to the brim at once and the whole place hears it happen.
activity: Find the coolest place in this village. Whoever lives there is the most important person here.
You find it: a covered passage behind the well. An old woman is already sitting in it and does not move.
incidents: A door opens, a bowl of water is thrown into the street, and the door closes.
The heat coming off a wall makes the far end of the street bend.

VillageIce.label: Winter Village
VillageIce.intro:
A village dug in for the winter. Paths cleared between the doors and nothing cleared beyond them.
The cold has made everybody's world about ninety metres across.
question: Nobody here has left this circle since November. Everybody here is very sick of each other.
Six months of the same forty people. Could you?
romantic: She stands in the cleared path between two houses where the snow is higher than both your heads.
They dug this so they could get to each other. That is all it is for.
Nobody has ever dug through anything to reach me. I would notice.
VillageIce.chaotic: Every roof in the village sheds its snow at once, in one enormous soft collapse, and the village is briefly invisible.
activity: Follow the paths and see whose door everybody's leads to. Somebody here is the centre of it.
You trace the cleared paths. They all converge on one door, and it is not the largest house.
incidents: Somebody's chimney gives out a burst of sparks and a smell of something burnt.
Two people meet on a path, say four words, and part.

VillageMountain.label: Mountain Village
VillageMountain.intro:
A village stuck to a slope, where every street is also a staircase.
Everything here was carried up by somebody.
question: Every stone in this place was carried up that road by hand. Every single one.
Why here? Nobody ever gives a good answer and everybody has one.
romantic: She sits on a step halfway up the village with the whole valley opening out below the roofs.
They built up here for a reason nobody alive remembers and they stayed for a different one.
Staying for a different reason than you came. I understand that one completely.
VillageMountain.chaotic: Every shutter on the mountain side of the village bangs open at once, and the valley hands the sound back four times.
activity: Climb to the top of the village with me. There is always a bench up there and it always has the best view.
There is a bench at the top. It has the best view and somebody's name on a small brass plate.
incidents: A bell rings down in the valley and arrives here about a second late.
Someone comes down the steps past you carrying something far too heavy and refuses help.

VillageRiver.label: River Village
VillageRiver.intro:
A village along a river, with everything important built on the wrong side of it.
There is a bridge, and there is an argument about the bridge.
question: Two halves of one village with a river down the middle. They have been separate for three centuries.
Which side would you have been born on? It matters here more than anything else about you.
romantic: She stops in the middle of the bridge, which is neither side, and stays there.
Both halves think the other half started it and both of them are right.
I usually start it. It is nice to be somewhere that managed it without me.
VillageRiver.chaotic: Every boat tied along the village breaks its rope at once and drifts downstream in perfect formation.
activity: Cross and come back. I want to see if anything changes about you.
You cross and come back. On the far bank a woman greets you and on this one nobody does.
incidents: Something is shouted from one bank to the other, twice, and not answered.
A boat goes past under the bridge with nobody visible in it.

VillageSea.label: Fishing Village
VillageSea.intro:
A fishing village with the boats up and the nets out to dry.
Everybody here is either at sea, waiting for somebody at sea, or retired from it.
question: Every house here faces the water. Not the road. The water.
Would you wait for somebody like that? Every day, on a wall?
romantic: She sits on the harbour wall facing out, in the place that has clearly been sat in for two hundred years.
The stone here is worn into a dip. Somebody has been waiting in this exact spot since before your language settled.
Being waited for is the thing I understand least and want most.
VillageSea.chaotic: Every net in the village untangles itself, all at once, perfectly, which will ruin four reputations.
activity: Read the boat names with me. Fishermen name boats after the person they are frightened of losing.
You read every hull in the harbour. Three of them have the same name and it is nobody's you can find.
incidents: A boat comes in late and everybody on the front counts the people in it without appearing to.
A gull takes something out of somebody's hand at the far end of the quay.

Volcano.label: Volcano
Volcano.intro:
The flank of a live volcano, warm underfoot and smelling of the inside of the world.
Something down there is audible and is not in a hurry.
question: This will kill everybody living on it eventually and every single one of them knows.
They stay because the soil is good. Is that brave or is it stupid?
romantic: She sits down on ground that is warmer than she is and does not appear to notice.
Everything that ever grew well grew on top of something that had gone catastrophically wrong.
I have gone catastrophically wrong several times. I keep waiting for the good soil.
Volcano.chaotic: The mountain clears its throat. Nothing erupts, but every bird on the flank leaves at the same moment.
activity: Get closer with me. Not stupidly closer. Just closer than we should.
You go closer than is sensible. The heat is a wall and neither of you turns round first.
incidents: The ground gives one deep knock, like something turning over in its sleep.
A vent puts out a plume that leans over the two of you and then decides otherwise.
